raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Since #45424, `import vllm` resolves `current_platform` and loads platform plugins while vLLM is still half-imported, because `PIN_MEMORY` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` is computed at import time. This PR computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access, so `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform, as `vllm/platforms/__init__.py` requires. Same root cause as #48397; #48444 fixed only that issue's WSL symptom.

## Claims

- `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform. The resolver runs 0 times during `import vllm`, down from 1.
- An out-of-tree platform plugin whose `register()` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`, directly or through another vLLM module, is detected again. Before this change it failed with `cannot import name ... from partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`, and vLLM silently fell back to another platform.
- `PIN_MEMORY` keeps its value. All `from vllm.utils.torch_utils import PIN_MEMORY` sites and monkeypatches (e.g. `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`) keep working.

## Validation

The existing dummy platform plugin's `register()` now imports a vLLM module, as real plugins do. A new subprocess test checks that `import vllm` leaves the platform unresolved and that the plugin platform still wins.

```bash
pip install -e tests/plugins/vllm_add_dummy_platform
pytest -v tests/plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py
```

| Check | main + new tests | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py`, CPU, rebased on current main | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| same, CUDA (L4)\* | 2 failed, 1 passed (`Expected DummyDevice, got cuda`) | 3 passed |
| resolver calls during `import vllm` (L4)\* | 1 | 0 |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (CPU) | 34 passed, 1 failed | 34 passed, 1 failed (same unrelated test) |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (L4)\* | — | 38 passed |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` greedy smoke run (L4)\* | — | OK, `PIN_MEMORY=True` on CUDA |

\* The L4 rows were run on an earlier base, 9dba339; I couldn't get GPU capacity to re-run them on current main. They also used an earlier version of the test, in which the dummy plugin imported `vllm.config`. On current main that import also runs into the separate `compilation.py` resolution described below, so the PR imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils` instead. The `torch_utils.py` change is identical, and no commits since 9dba339 touch `torch_utils.py`, `env_override.py`, `platform_utils.py` or `platforms/__init__.py`.

<details>
<summary>Fake out-of-tree plugin matrix (L4): 4 plugin styles × 4 first-import styles</summary>

**Plugin styles.** `register()` does one of:
- imports nothing;
- `import vllm.config`;
- `from vllm.config import VllmConfig`;
- nothing, but the platform module imports `vllm.config` at top level.

**First imports:** `import vllm`, `from vllm import LLM`, `EngineArgs`, `import vllm.config`.

| | cells not OK |
|---|---|
| main | 12/16 (plugin replaced by `NvmlCudaPlatform`, or `ImportError ... partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`) |
| this PR | 4/16 |
| before #45424 | 4/16 (same cells) |

The remaining 4 cells come from `vllm/config/compilation.py:22`, which resolves the platform during `import vllm.config`. That predates #45424 and is out of scope here.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main):
1. `vllm/__init__.py:14` imports `vllm.env_override`.
2. `vllm/env_override.py:153` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`.
3. `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py:76` runs `PIN_MEMORY = is_pin_memory_available()`.
4. `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py:45` imports `current_platform`, which resolves the platform and loads plugins.

This happens while `torch_utils` has only run up to line 76. A plugin that imports vLLM in `register()` gets an `ImportError`. Detection swallows it (`vllm/platforms/__init__.py`, `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname`), so vLLM falls back to another platform and caches that platform's pin-memory setting.

**Fix.** A module `__getattr__` (PEP 562) computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access and stores it as a module global, so later reads are plain global lookups. The three uses inside `torch_utils.py` go through `_pin_memory()`, which also honours an assigned or monkeypatched `PIN_MEMORY`.

**Why the existing plugin test missed this.** The dummy plugin's `register()` imported nothing from vLLM, and the test only checks the final `device_name`. Also, the Plugin Tests CI step only triggers on changes under `vllm/plugins/` and `tests/plugins/`, so it did not run for #45424. It does run for this PR. Adding `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` / `vllm/env_override.py` to that step's `source_file_dependencies` would catch future regressions; I left it out to keep CI load unchanged, but can add it if maintainers prefer.

**Alternative considered.** Move `is_torch_equal*` out of `torch_utils`, so `env_override` no longer imports it (3 files, +68/-51). That also fixes `import vllm`, but it leaves the import-time platform resolution in `torch_utils` for the next early importer.

**Duplicate check.** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `PIN_MEMORY`, `is_pin_memory_available`, `current_platform` + `import vllm`, `platform plugin circular import` and `partially initialized module torch_utils`. Only related, none open: #48397 / #48444 (WSL symptom of the same root cause) and #52285 (logging of detection failures).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write and test this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.

detail.body:
## Overview

Since #45424, `import vllm` resolves `current_platform` and loads platform plugins while vLLM is still half-imported, because `PIN_MEMORY` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` is computed at import time. This PR computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access, so `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform, as `vllm/platforms/__init__.py` requires. Same root cause as #48397; #48444 fixed only that issue's WSL symptom.

## Claims

- `import vllm` no longer resolves the platform. The resolver runs 0 times during `import vllm`, down from 1.
- An out-of-tree platform plugin whose `register()` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`, directly or through another vLLM module, is detected again. Before this change it failed with `cannot import name ... from partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`, and vLLM silently fell back to another platform.
- `PIN_MEMORY` keeps its value. All `from vllm.utils.torch_utils import PIN_MEMORY` sites and monkeypatches (e.g. `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`) keep working.

## Validation

The existing dummy platform plugin's `register()` now imports a vLLM module, as real plugins do. A new subprocess test checks that `import vllm` leaves the platform unresolved and that the plugin platform still wins.

```bash
pip install -e tests/plugins/vllm_add_dummy_platform
pytest -v tests/plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py
pytest tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py
```

| Check | main + new tests | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py`, CPU, rebased on current main | 1 failed, 2 passed | 3 passed |
| same, CUDA (L4)\* | 2 failed, 1 passed (`Expected DummyDevice, got cuda`) | 3 passed |
| resolver calls during `import vllm` (L4)\* | 1 | 0 |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (CPU) | 34 passed, 1 failed | 34 passed, 1 failed (same unrelated test) |
| `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` (L4)\* | — | 38 passed |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` greedy smoke run (L4)\* | — | OK, `PIN_MEMORY=True` on CUDA |

\* The L4 rows were run on an earlier base, 9dba339; I couldn't get GPU capacity to re-run them on current main. They also used an earlier version of the test, in which the dummy plugin imported `vllm.config`. On current main that import also runs into the separate `compilation.py` resolution described below, so the PR imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils` instead. The `torch_utils.py` change is identical, and no commits since 9dba339 touch `torch_utils.py`, `env_override.py`, `platform_utils.py` or `platforms/__init__.py`.

<details>
<summary>Fake out-of-tree plugin matrix (L4): 4 plugin styles × 4 first-import styles</summary>

**Plugin styles.** `register()` does one of:
- imports nothing;
- `import vllm.config`;
- `from vllm.config import VllmConfig`;
- nothing, but the platform module imports `vllm.config` at top level.

**First imports:** `import vllm`, `from vllm import LLM`, `EngineArgs`, `import vllm.config`.

| | cells not OK |
|---|---|
| main | 12/16 (plugin replaced by `NvmlCudaPlatform`, or `ImportError ... partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'`) |
| this PR | 4/16 |
| before #45424 | 4/16 (same cells) |

The remaining 4 cells come from `vllm/config/compilation.py:22`, which resolves the platform during `import vllm.config`. That predates #45424 and is out of scope here.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main):
1. `vllm/__init__.py:14` imports `vllm.env_override`.
2. `vllm/env_override.py:153` imports `vllm.utils.torch_utils`.
3. `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py:76` runs `PIN_MEMORY = is_pin_memory_available()`.
4. `vllm/utils/platform_utils.py:45` imports `current_platform`, which resolves the platform and loads plugins.

This happens while `torch_utils` has only run up to line 76. A plugin that imports vLLM in `register()` gets an `ImportError`. Detection swallows it (`vllm/platforms/__init__.py`, `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname`), so vLLM falls back to another platform and caches that platform's pin-memory setting.

**Fix.** A module `__getattr__` (PEP 562) computes `PIN_MEMORY` on first access and stores it as a module global, so later reads are plain global lookups. The three uses inside `torch_utils.py` go through `_pin_memory()`, which also honours an assigned or monkeypatched `PIN_MEMORY`.

**Why the existing plugin test missed this.** The dummy plugin's `register()` imported nothing from vLLM, and the test only checks the final `device_name`. Also, the Plugin Tests CI step only triggers on changes under `vllm/plugins/` and `tests/plugins/`, so it did not run for #45424. It does run for this PR. Adding `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` / `vllm/env_override.py` to that step's `source_file_dependencies` would catch future regressions; I left it out to keep CI load unchanged, but can add it if maintainers prefer.

**Alternative considered.** Move `is_torch_equal*` out of `torch_utils`, so `env_override` no longer imports it (3 files, +68/-51). That also fixes `import vllm`, but it leaves the import-time platform resolution in `torch_utils` for the next early importer.

**Duplicate check.** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `PIN_MEMORY`, `is_pin_memory_available`, `current_platform` + `import vllm`, `platform plugin circular import` and `partially initialized module torch_utils`. Only related, none open: #48397 / #48444 (WSL symptom of the same root cause) and #52285 (logging of detection failures).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to investigate, write and test this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
